items.prompt: A single ATR 42-600 twin-engine turboprop regional airliner, completely unpainted: pure clean white fuselage, wings and tail, with absolutely no livery, no logos, no airline titles, no registration and no cheatline. Exact aircraft identity, follow every point: overall length 22.67 metres, wingspan 24.57 metres (wingspan noticeably longer than the fuselage, a very short stubby fuselage under a long wing -- shorter and stubbier than the larger ATR 72), fuselage diameter 2.87 metres, total height 7.59 metres. HIGH-MOUNTED WINGS sitting on top of the fuselage, unswept and straight, no winglets, plain rounded wingtips. A T-TAIL: horizontal stabiliser mounted at the very top of the swept vertical fin, well clear of the propeller wash. Two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW127 turboprop engines mounted on the leading edge of the high wing, each driving a SIX-BLADE PROPELLER (thin, slightly scimitar-curved blades, large spinner cone) -- no jet nacelle, this is a propeller aircraft. The main landing gear does NOT retract into the engine nacelles or the wing: it retracts into distinctive teardrop-shaped fairings (sponsons) low on the fuselage sides, near the belly -- the same signature ATR recognition feature as the larger ATR 72. Twin-wheel nose gear under the cockpit. Two passenger doors, small round cabin windows in a four-abreast single-aisle cabin -- noticeably fewer windows than the ATR 72 since the cabin is shorter. Blunt rounded nose, straightforward two-pilot cockpit glazing.
